items.title: What Marx predicted
items.claim: Karl Marx predicted that capitalism would generate growing inequality and eventual crisis. Recent empirical work (Piketty, 2014) examined wealth concentration over centuries. What was a headline finding?

options.text: Wealth inequality has steadily fallen since 1800
When the rate of return on capital exceeds growth, wealth concentrates
Inequality is impossible to measure historically

items.reveal_title: r greater than g concentrates wealth
items.reveal:
Piketty's Capital in the Twenty-First Century (2014) used tax records across France, UK, US and others to argue that when the return on capital (r) exceeds the economic growth rate (g), inherited wealth grows faster than earned income.

The book's data and conclusions remain contested but reopened debates Marx began.
items.why: Empirical historical economics revived classical sociological questions about class structure.

items.title: UK household structure today
items.claim: What proportion of UK households in 2022 were single-person households according to the Office for National Statistics?
items.reveal_title: Roughly three in ten UK households are one person
items.reveal:
ONS data for 2022 reported around 30% of households contained a single person. The figure has risen steadily since the 1960s.

The 'standard' nuclear family is now a minority household type.
items.why: Demographic change reshapes assumptions built into policy and earlier sociological theory.

items.title: Disadvantage gap in England
items.claim: England's 'disadvantage gap' tracks attainment of pupils eligible for free school meals against peers. After narrowing in the 2010s, what happened from 2019?

options.text: It widened, including after pandemic disruption
It reversed: FSM pupils overtook peers

items.reveal:
Education Policy Institute analyses reported the disadvantage gap at GCSE widened from 2019, reaching its widest in over a decade by 2022.

Pandemic-related school closures appear to have amplified pre-existing trends.
items.why: Apparent progress can reverse when systems are stressed, revealing structural fragility.
